summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis was admitted for severe abdominal pain, elevated white blood cell count, and recent constipation. Initial imaging showed no acute abdominal process but revealed severe hepatomegaly and stool burden. A stool test confirmed Clostridium difficile infection, which was treated with oral vancomycin and IV metronidazole. Her leukocytosis resolved, diarrhea improved, and abdominal pain subsided. Amitiza was discontinued due to contribution to diarrhea, and diuretics were held due to hypotension but planned for outpatient restart. She remained stable, with controlled hepatic encephalopathy and ongoing management of iron deficiency anemia. She was discharged home with a tapering course of vancomycin, instructions to follow up with her liver and primary care teams, and guidance on when to resume diuretics.
problems: Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
